usageNotes: Use this to update metadata or settings on an existing API token — such as adjusting its expiration date, toggling privilege separation, or updating a comment. When 'regenerate' is set, the response is the only opportunity to capture the new token secret; it cannot be retrieved again after this call. Callers must either own the token (self) or hold User.Modify on the user's group.

examples.summary: Rotate the secret for a monitoring service account token and extend its expiration by one year

tips: Capture the 'value' field from the response immediately when 'regenerate' is true — it is returned only once and cannot be retrieved via any subsequent GET.
The full tokenid string used in Authorization headers is '<userid>!<tokenid>' (e.g., 'monitoring@pve!grafana-ro'); the 'full-tokenid' field in the response provides this when regenerating.
Setting 'privsep': false grants the token all of the user's own privileges — use only for tightly scoped service accounts where ACL management overhead outweighs risk.
To clear an optional field (e.g., remove a comment or reset expiration to 'same as user'), pass its name in the 'delete' param as a comma-separated config-id list.
Regenerating invalidates the old secret immediately; coordinate rotation with all consumers before calling to avoid service interruption.
